about:
Savannah Food Company, based in Savannah, Tennessee, traces its roots to 1970 when Bob Hagy, after decades in the restaurant business, began producing hushpuppies from his family’s recipes. The Catfish Hotel Restaurant, still operating today, had built a reputation for its freshly made hushpuppies, prompting Hagy to build a dedicated processing facility. In 2004, the company was acquired by John Bryan, whose family had founded Bryan Foods, Inc., in the early 1900s.

The facility manufactures a line of frozen hushpuppies — Original, Jalapeño, and Sweet Corn — along with other Southern-style side dishes. Production follows a strict hazard analysis and critical control point (HACCP) plan, good manufacturing practices (GMP), and global food safety initiative (GFSI) benchmarks. The plant has held FSSC 22000 certification since June 2013, aligning with ISO-based food safety standards.

The company sells its products through retail stores, as indicated by a store locator on its website, distributing under the Savannah Classics brand.

The business emphasizes its commitment to food safety and quality, citing its FSSC 22000 certification, HACCP/GMP/GFSI systems, and the use of high-quality ingredients to replicate scratch-made flavor. The operation was built on family recipes passed down through generations, aiming to deliver products as good as homemade.
